answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: No idea honestly. It sounds like dry paperwork, maybe a legal or recruitment term, or a game about a job contract or being officially appointed. I'd guess it's a serious, boring office sim with little drama, and I wouldn't know what the words mean in context.

answer.held_back_by: Honestly nothing held me back, I got to PM. If anything the game held back the drama: honesty kept winning, so the stakes felt low. The rival, the credit-stealer, the Y13 board seat, the winking woman and the Y11 quote I flagged never came back, as far as I saw.
answer.ending_fair_why: I picked honest and ambitious options every time and got PM with integrity at 100, which matches. The declassified card explaining the ceiling and the Reshuffle was a nice reveal. I'd have liked some payoff for the Tuesday man though.
answer.chase_next: I'd try the compromised route: take the conglomerate board seat, stay silent when the Director asks if the system is a joke, and see if I can crash and burn or get a scandal ending. I want to see what the game does when honesty isn't the winning move.
answer.play_again_why: I enjoyed the pay committee arc, but the later decades repeated the same choices and many threads I set up went nowhere. I'd come back after a break to try the dishonest route, not right now.

tone_breaks.line: Game mentioned a 'young family' I never set up.
tone_breaks.note: Felt like a continuity slip, as it mentioned a family I never chose.

tone_breaks.line: YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
tone_breaks.note: I don't know how real civil service files work, so I can't judge accuracy. It was also a hidden mechanic I only learned about at the end.

answer.title_fit_why: The pay formula, the pay committee and the bonus tied to indicators ran through the whole game and the ending opens on the salary, so it fits better than a title about being confirmed, which I never understood in the game.
